newsitem.title: UK: British Gas down as bid hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: British Gas down as bid hopes fade.

text.p: Shares in British Gas Plc dropped on Wednesday after a press report that oil group Shell had ruled out a bid for the company.

British Gas shares were down 7-1/2p at 223-1/2 by 0929 GMT, also depressed by tax changes in yesterday's Budget that would cut capital allowances on long-life assts. Such changes were seen as particularly costly for utilities.

Another negative for British Gas today was press comment that suggested the company could suffer tighter regulatory scrutiny following National Grid Plc's settlement with electricity industry watchdog Offer.

The Financial Times Lex column said British Gas could expect tougher treatment from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission after National Grid on Tuesday delivered higher cost cuts than it had originally told Offer were achievable.
Today's decline came after British Gas shares rose sharply earlier this month on an outbreak of bid speculation.
Yet a report in the Independent newspaper said Royal Dutch/Shell Group chairman Cor Herkstroter said the company was not interested in a bid for British Gas.
"British Gas shares rose very quickly last week on the back of a story that Shell is going to bid for the company," said Irene Himona, analyst at SocGen.
"It was a fairly silly story in the first place and last night the chairman confirmed there is no way Shell is going to bid and that's why it's coming off."
Trading in British Gas shares was active and volume reached 8.4 million shares by 1009 GMT, making it the most active stock in the London market.
